title: Preserve enrollment contracts while making future official Quest Expression optional

source.ref: Daniel's November 14, 2026 authorization to complete the support/practice/expression changeover with three review passes.

detail: Local implementation snapshots version 2 only on future official ranked fixed-window enrollments; NULL legacy and unenrolled participation keep their existing qualification. The same 14-day bar and current rank eligibility remain; Expression becomes optional only under the recorded new contract. Oldest active policy wins, with deterministic ties and newest-completed retry selection. The database freezes future full support IDs at actual log insertion, preserves them through partial-to-full/reward updates and practice deletion, rejects caller-forged snapshot meaning, and never backfills historical third/fourth supports. Prospective reads use bounded monotonic ID keysets until empty, distinguish provider/error incompleteness, use the server-resolved member day, and count a date once. Missing historical secondary shares keep known primary credit while marking unknown evidence; UI labels this as a lower bound and allows completion on 14 known days. V2 Expression controls remain available before and after Journey completion without claiming an unperformed Expression was done; default legacy action text is unchanged. The unchanged new consequence probe failed against main9fd87ee37 at the actual optional-policy qualification assertion and passes locally. Focused verification passed 90 tests across ten files including unchanged legacy completion and reward tests; changed-file lint across 14 source files passed. Actual isolated PGlite PostgreSQL replayed the new migration three times with 23 assertions passing. Twenty-four new pgTAP staging cases require full isolated Supabase replay and real API readiness before release. Real components rendered with synthetic owner data at all five required widths, without overflow or unnamed controls; this is not authenticated acceptance. SQL51000 remains local and unapplied behind the existing migration line; no PR, production SQL, email, reward-value, flag, grant-key or earned-recognition change was performed. This row records implementation consequences, not production activation. A standalone local-only Auth/PostgREST acceptance script uses local CLI credentials exclusively, refuses hosted/routed/credentialed URLs and redirects, bounds requests, and cleans partial fixtures and Auth users; twelve safety/cleanup tests pass. Actual HTTP acceptance is not claimed until full isolated Supabase staging executes it. Finished V2 rendering uses actual challenge existence so a missing challenge cannot produce an unusable action; real asynchronous server-component wiring tests cover this, legacy rendering, and signed-out omission. Final local backlog contract passed with 2684 entries and 991 agreeing probes; the unchanged exact SCAN-502 guard passed at 150 exports. Root and independent peer code reviews passed after correcting provider short-page truncation and actual challenge existence in finished V2 rendering. Current-main composition on 69a6c5af5 preserves the original legacy primary-category fan-out and independently reads owner-scoped recorded V2 enrollment candidates using the resolved log day. Bounded monotonic keysets continue through provider-short pages to an empty page; duplicate plans reuse the same authoritative completion evaluator and existing reward keys. Read failures report a fixed reason without private payloads and do not break logging. Completed-enrollment candidates remain bounded to the recorded window, not unlimited cross-season payout retries. The actual untouched baseline checked Body but omitted the Mind Journey after a mixed-support log; the unchanged new fan-out probe captures the missing route. Root source hashes and independent policy review agreed before transfer. In the current container, 119 focused tests across 12 files and 16 changed TypeScript files lint pass; both frozen probes pass with their original bytes. SQL SHA-256 remains ec30f6f342bbd51ed693e15b16c7b2da79b4eded6f59a8ec03d7e2c249efe491. Real disposable Supabase staging stopped before migration replay when Docker VFS image startup exhausted disk; cleanup restored free space, and the 24 new pgTAP assertions and authenticated HTTP acceptance remain unexecuted. No full staging success, production application or activation is claimed. Final current-main composition required backlog passes with 2690 entries and 997 agreeing probes; the dead-export report remains exactly 150 against the unchanged 150 ceiling. Both immutable probe hashes and the migration hash remain unchanged. Serial migration inventory on November 14 now reserves version 47000 for open FH-018S and 48000 for open PROG-E9. This unpublished, unapplied candidate is mechanically renamed to 20270346049000_quest_support_policy.sql; all migration bytes and both frozen Quest probes remain identical. Current main f4f21ebe75 was normally merged, retaining landed support readers, guidance, picker and pagination. The LIVE-2294 activation filename references were subsequently corrected in this own feature during the51000 queue retiming; its reader flag stays off. No production migration application or SQL publication is performed. After that normal merge and byte-identical migration rename, all 119 focused tests across 12 files and 16 changed TypeScript lint checks pass again; both immutable probes remain green and the exact dead-export report stays at 150. Required backlog passes with 2695 entries and 1002 agreeing probes. Quest HTTP workflow insertion is prepared outside the repository only, after the existing analytics experiment acceptance and before unconditional cleanup; it is not applied, dispatched or registered yet. Authorized queue correction after main bce47c132 restores the already-applied Loom48000 application to main: analytics is being retimed to version50000 ahead of Quest. The still-local, unapplied Quest migration is mechanically renamed from49000 to51000 with the same ec30f6 SQL byte hash. Related default-off reader activation references in .env.example and RUNBOOKS now point to51000 so they cannot confuse the distinct Loom48000 migration. This changes documentation only, leaves PRACTICE_SUPPORT_EVIDENCE_ENABLED blank/off, and does not apply SQL or activate the reader. The old49000 reservation is superseded; future staging/registration must use51000. Quest HTTP workflow insertion remains an external proposal until the analytics50000 workflow is on main. Verification after merging main bce47c132 and retiming to51000: the same 119 focused tests across 12 files, 16 changed TypeScript lint checks and both unchanged frozen Quest probes pass. No existing tests, probe assertions, migration bytes or rollout flag values were changed. Required backlog and real isolated staging must be refreshed after the pending analytics workflow lands and the final Quest HTTP step is composed; no stale earlier staging is claimed for this head.
